issue_context.title: Restarting a failing socket unit repeatedly only triggers `OnFailure=` dependency the first time
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

255.14-1.fc40

### Used distribution

Fedora 40

### Linux kernel version used

6.11.11-200.fc40.x86_64

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

(Re)starting a socket unit whose which will fail should retrigger the `OnFailure=` handler

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

The `OnFailure=` handler is only triggered the first the the unit enters the failed state. Subsequent invocations no longer trigger the respective handler

### Steps to reproduce the problem

Create the following units:

```ini
# /run/user/1000/systemd/user/test.socket
[Unit]
OnSuccess=handler@s.service
OnFailure=handler@f.service

[Socket]
; unprivileged user will not be able to bind to this port
ListenStream=10

# /run/user/1000/systemd/user/handler@.service
[Service]
ExecStart=env
```

Afterwards, repeatedly run `systemctl restart --user test.socket`. Inspect the journal (`journalctl --user --since=10m\ ago -t systemd`) to see that the handler is only invoked once.  `systemctl reset-failed --user test.socket` will reset the unit state and a subsequent invocation will again trigger the failure handler once.

### Additional program output to the terminal or log subsystem illustrating the issue

```sh
test.socket: Failed to create listening socket ([::]:10): Permission denied
test.socket: Failed to listen on sockets: Permission denied
test.socket: Failed with result 'resources'.
Failed to listen on test.socket.
test.socket: Triggering OnFailure= dependencies.
Started handler@f.service.
test.socket: Failed to create listening socket ([::]:10): Permission denied
test.socket: Failed to listen on sockets: Permission denied
test.socket: Failed with result 'resources'.
Failed to listen on test.socket.
test.socket: Failed to create listening socket ([::]:10): Permission denied
test.socket: Failed to listen on sockets: Permission denied
test.socket: Failed with result 'resources'.
Failed to listen on test.socket.
test.socket: Failed to create listening socket ([::]:10): Permission denied
test.socket: Failed to listen on sockets: Permission denied
test.socket: Failed with result 'resources'.
Failed to listen on test.socket.
```

review_comments:
I'd like to insert an assertion about socket state, something like the following (though not checked carefully):
```c
assert(IN_SET(s->state, SOCKET_DEAD, SOCKET_FAILED, SOCKET_START_PRE));
```
Hmm, dunno. I added assert in `socket_enter_start_chown` because it depends on `_OPEN`. But here exists no strict dep/relationship between these states.
Not checked in detail, but is it safe to call it accidentally when in other states, e.g. by already started socket?
